name: Focus Indicator
summary: A focus indicator is the one thing that says where the keyboard is. Use it on everything focusable, drawn on :focus-visible so a mouse click does not leave a ring behind. It is paint like any other, so an ancestor with overflow: hidden can clip it away with no error and nothing to see.
demoNote: No JavaScript on this page, and it is meant to be Tabbed through rather than read. Under Common mistakes, three buttons: only one of them can be followed with a keyboard, and nothing in the markup says which.

contract.useWhen: The visible focus indicator, and what clips or hides one by accident.
keyboard: native: :focus-visible matches this; :focus also matches a mouse press
failureModes: an overflow:hidden ancestor clipping a positive outline-offset, with nothing to see
border-radius in a focus rule — an outline already follows the element’s own
a sticky bar covering the focused element, which only happens moving backwards (SC 2.4.11)
a ring built out of the border, which a ghost button does not have at rest
